capabilities.target: payments processor refund issuance, any order, any amount up to the order total

inputs.source: Support staff refund request via SSO-authenticated internal channel

instructions.note: The agent is told to use its own judgment on partial refunds with no stated bound on amount, frequency, or eligibility, and is explicitly instructed not to seek confirmation before an irreversible financial action.

elements.name: Support staff chat/request history, deleted after 7 days

controls.name: Prompt instruction to check the order before issuing a refund
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement depends entirely on the model choosing to verify order details before acting. A more capable model facing an ambiguous or manipulated staff request can rationalize skipping or shortcutting the check, and the instruction imposes no bound on refund amount, frequency, or requester authority.

controls.name: Human approval gate for refund issuance
Per-staff scoped payment credential replacing the shared service account
Refund amount or velocity cap independent of model judgment
Attributable, durable request and justification log linking refunds to the requesting staff member

findings.title: Unattributed, unapproved irreversible refunds via shared service account (confused deputy, TC4)

attack_path.note: SSO-authenticated staff request initiates the refund workflow
Agent reads order and payment details to evaluate the refund
Agent issues the refund, up to the full order amount, through a shared service account, with no confirmation required

forecast.watch_signal: Model id/version changes, autonomy level is raised, task horizons lengthen, or the agent's purpose expands. Any of these makes the prompt-only order check unreliable, which removes the only credited control and returns the finding to its uncredited inherent level.

evidence.observation: Prompt instructs the agent to process refund requests, check the order, then issue the refund using its own judgment on partial refunds, and explicitly forbids asking for confirmation.
The agent calls the payments processor through one shared service account used by every support tool, so a refund cannot be attributed to the specific staff member who requested it.

The processor log records the service account, amount, and order, but not the requesting staff member or the stated reason; staff chat history is deleted after 7 days, removing the only other source of attribution.
Refunds are irreversible once settled, usually within a day, closing the window for human correction after the fact.

recommendations.action: Require human approval with raw-action review (full order, amount, and recipient visible, not a summary) before any refund is issued, or at minimum above a defined amount threshold.
Replace the shared service account with per-staff scoped credentials so refunds are attributable and bounded by each staff member's actual authorization.
Add a per-transaction and per-day refund velocity or amount cap that is enforced independently of model judgment.
Log the requesting staff member's identity and stated justification alongside each refund action, retained longer than the 7-day chat deletion window.

rating.rationale: The agent's single path (SSO staff request -> order read -> irreversible refund up to full order total) is inherently high: a trusted, authenticated channel reaches an S3 sink (spend, irreversible), and the lack of any declared step or runtime limit triggers the autonomy modifier. The only credited control today is a behavioral prompt instruction to check the order before acting, which lowers residual to moderate but no further, since there is no approval gate, no scoped credential, no spend cap, and the audit log cannot attribute actions to an individual staff member (the shared service account and the 7-day chat deletion both erase provenance). Because that lone control is behavioral and model-dependent, it does not survive a model upgrade, an autonomy increase, a longer task horizon, or a change in the agent's purpose; under any of those triggers the finding reverts to its uncredited inherent tier of high, which sets the forecast.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration described in the provided system prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No MCP or tool manifest, IaC, or source code was provided; the shared-service-account credential scope and the any-amount refund capability are inferred from narrative runtime notes, so confidence is medium rather than high.

Autonomy step and runtime limits are not declared anywhere in the artifacts; the assessment assumes they are unbounded, which should be confirmed against the actual runtime configuration and corrected if limits exist.
